scope: author self-report; not independent acceptance evidence
messages:
I’ll build a cohesive neon racing game directly in Studio, then test the driving loop, progression, and compact UI. I’ll prioritize a playable race and server-owned progression while filling out the garage, shop, and social systems.
The neon harbor and circuit are in place. I’m connecting the kart simulation to a server-owned wallet and loadout, so purchases, upgrades, rewards, and race results all feed the same progression loop.
The main systems are connected: kart selection and upgrades, parts, driver rentals, livery, crates, rewards, codes, quests, and demo parties. I’m moving into Play testing now, focusing first on runtime errors, the voting-to-race transition, and whether the interface remains usable on small screens.
Play testing found and fixed two startup errors. The queue, live voting, and race camera now run. I’m testing a full three-lap finish and improving world lighting, controller focus, and panel layering before the final device checks.
A full race completed and awarded credits, crystals, XP, and a race count exactly once. Shop cancellation left the wallet unchanged, and a confirmed motor purchase updated it correctly. I also found keyboard focus was swallowing acceleration; driving now uses a higher-priority native input binding.
The keyboard race test now finishes correctly, including boost and steering, with a first-place result. I also checked the interface at a 390-pixel portrait width: navigation scrolls horizontally, panels remain usable, and canceling a livery discard preserves the draft. I’m tightening the remaining timer displays and controller Back/focus behavior.
The race-to-hub loop is working with rewards and loadout intact. Server checks also passed for upgrades, rentals, free crates, duplicate daily claims, code redemption, and demo party replies. The circuit now includes alternating energy gates that reward steering with boost energy and credits.
